A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLAUSE framework and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends after the references despite unresolved appendix references; v2 supplies Appendices A–H. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA accuracy, latency, edge usage, constraint-satisfaction experiments, agent ablations and a case study in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations using two alternative reader models in Appendix D, Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The edit–traverse–curate workflow, learned stopping, edge scoring, multi-head critic and resource-specific dual updates remain unchanged. Expanded anchoring descriptions and Appendix C pseudocode document the existing procedure without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both evaluate HotpotQA distractor, FactKG and MetaQA 1/2/3-hop. Appendix D newly describes their underlying graphs. Alternative readers change model configurations, and Appendix F discusses scalability without adding an evaluated dataset or graph-noise scenario.

E2.justification: The standalone LLMs, four RAG methods, four agent methods and MAPPO/fixed-penalty PPO/RCPO comparisons are retained. Tables 8–9 reuse the existing RAG and agent comparator sets with different readers; the newly supplied LightRAG citation does not introduce a new baseline.

E3.justification: Tables 8–9 introduce LLaMA3.3-70B and GPT-OSS-120B reader configurations for CLAUSE and the existing RAG/agent comparisons. The original Qwen3-32B evaluation, metrics and normalization remain unchanged. Newly disclosed token, hop and candidate-pool defaults do not establish changes to earlier experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a reader-backbone sensitivity check, testing whether CLAUSE's advantage persists with larger alternative readers. The original agent/dual ablations and Brian Backer case study retain their findings. The scalability discussion supplies no additional empirical robustness test.

E5.justification: Figure 2 already reports mean ± SD in v1 and remains unchanged. v2 supplies no actual seed values, run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Its statement that seeds accompany a supplementary archive adds access documentation without specifying a changed statistical practice.

E6.justification: All original benchmark and ablation values are retained in v2 Tables 2–5. New Tables 8–9 substantially extend the results across alternative readers: CLAUSE reports HotpotQA EM@1 of 73.5 with LLaMA3.3-70B and 75.0 with GPT-OSS-120B. These are additional experimental conditions, not same-setting improvements over the retained Qwen3-32B score of 71.7.

T1.justification: v1 asserts shadow-price and convergence properties but supplies no referenced appendices. v2 adds time/space complexity derivations in Appendices E–F, a shadow-price proposition in G, and assumptions A1–A6 with actor-convergence and dual/KKT arguments in H. This is substantial new formal content, although the convergence argument has correctness problems.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same budget-conditioned context-construction, three-agent coordination and accuracy–efficiency claims, including the same headline MetaQA comparison. Consolidating seven contribution bullets into four does not materially redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets the reader comparisons as narrowing the performance gap between medium and larger LLMs. Appendix F adds explanations of shared-encoder efficiency, local-frontier scalability and noise mitigation. Existing interpretations of the main experiments remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices C–F add pseudocode, hardware/software and API details, embedding/NER/indexing choices, KG construction and scale, and inference defaults including 512 tokens, four hops and a 128-item candidate pool. v2 also reports a supplementary code archive containing seeds and run scripts; its availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including LightRAG, Han et al. on step-by-step reading and Zhou on shared encoders, replaces the MetaQA citation to Puerto et al. with Zhang et al. (2018), and expands the positioning paragraph around four research families. Most other reference changes are bibliographic updates to existing works.

P1.justification: The exposition expands substantially through a reorganized problem formulation, fuller anchoring explanation, rewritten contribution and positioning passages, and structured Appendices A–H. Ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use disclosures are added, and unresolved appendix references are repaired. The main section sequence and much of the empirical narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two notation tables, a KG-statistics table, two reader-comparison tables and four algorithm displays. Existing result tables are renumbered and repositioned, with publication headers and revised page layout. Figures 1–4 retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: The implementation and KG details make the retained method easier to inspect, and Tables 8–9 strengthen evidence that its advantage persists across readers. However, the added theory does not reliably resolve v1's unsupported convergence claim: Appendix H.3 calls D(lambda)=max_theta L(theta,lambda) concave and invokes ascent, although this defined dual is convex in lambda. The documentation and empirical gains support a limited net improvement.
